title: Truth
lead: In the Hebrew Bible truth (emet) is reliability and faithfulness, above all God's; in Greek, alētheia is what is real and not false. The Bible calls God "faithful God" (Psalm 31:5), and the New Testament calls Jesus "the truth" (John 14:6). 1 Esdras makes truth the winner of a contest at the Persian court.

sections.b: The Hebrew emet comes from the root of amen, "firm, sure." It is used of true words, but most often of people and above all of God, who keeps his word (Exodus 34:6; Psalm 117:2). The Greek Old Testament usually renders it alētheia, a word that in Greek leans toward what is real as opposed to false or hidden. Both senses meet in the New Testament: God's word is truth (John 17:17), Jesus is "the way, the truth and the life" (John 14:6), and the Spirit leads into all truth (John 16:13). People can swap "the truth of God for the lie" (Romans 1:25).
